newsitem.title: LEBANON: 87 Lebanese sentenced for dealing with Israel.
newsitem.headline: 87 Lebanese sentenced for dealing with Israel.

text.p: Lebanon's military court has sentenced 87 Lebanese men each to 15 years in jail with hard labour for collaborating with Israel, court sources said.

The 87 defendants, who were sentenced in absentia late on Wednesday, live in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone. Under Lebanese law, people sentenced in absentia are retried when they surrender or are arrested.
The court said they "contacted the Israeli enemy and collaborated with it in the occupied security zone". It sentenced each of them to 15 years in jail with hard labour.
Among those sentenced was Aa'qil Hashim, who was identified as a senior official of the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia.
Lebanon and Israel are officially in a state of war and Lebanese laws forbid citizens from contacting or dealing with the Jewish state.
Last December Lebanon's military court sentenced to death in absentia the head of the SLA, General Antoine Lahd, on the same charges.

Israel has had its own forces and client Lebanese forces in south Lebanon since 1978. It currently occupies a 15-km (nine-mile) -wide strip of south Lebanon it says is needed to protect northern Israel.
